sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by tag-specific antibody detection on intact cells; constructs were used to study LY6D surface localisation. Functional impact on GPI-anchored protein activity not explicitly quantified in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: L1 and L2 both explicitly name the 20/21 junction as the insertion site in full-length, membrane-anchored LY6D. Python verification confirms residue 20 = T (last SP residue) and residue 21 = L (first mature-protein residue), consistent with the topology landmark (mature N-terminus = 21). The entire mature protein (residues 21–128) is extracellular in this GPI-anchored protein, so the tag sits on the extracellular face with no TM boundary proximity concern. L1 is cited as the primary construction record; L2 corroborates with the surface-accessibility rationale. Full-length LY6D expressed in mammalian cells (pcDNA3 vector); HA tag (YPYDVPDYA) and FLAG tag (DYKDDDDK) each inserted independently between residues 20 and 21 — immediately after the signal-peptide cleavage site — to generate 20HA-LY6D and 20Flag-LY6D constructs. The authors explicitly chose this junction because the signal sequence (residues 1–20) is cleaved upon ER entry, placing the tag at the mature extracellular N-terminus where it is accessible to tag-specific antibodies on the cell surface.

sources.claim: For the construction of LY6D containing an internal HA tag (20HA-LY6D) or Flag tag (20Flag-LY6D) between amino acid residues 20 and 21, DNA fragments corresponding to the 5’ of LY6D (1-60 bp), the HA (TACCCATACGACGTGCCAGACTACGCC) or Flag tag (GACTACAAAGACGATGACGACAAG) sequence, and the 3’ of LY6D (61-387 bp) were ligated in this order to the pcDNA3 vector by using the In-Fusion cloning system (Takara Bio, Shiga, Japan) to generate pcDNA3-20HA-LY6D and pcDNA3-20Flag-LY6D.

literature_notes: The ledger contains two clips (L1, L2) from the same paper (PMC7948989), both describing the identical 20/21 junction with HA and FLAG tags in full-length LY6D. No other junctions or loops are mentioned in the ledger. LY6D is a GPI-anchored Ly6/uPAR-family protein with no transmembrane domain; the entire mature sequence (residues 21–128) is extracellular. The signal peptide (residues 1–20) is cleaved, so the 20/21 junction is the only extracellular terminus available. No internal loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or other positions appear in the ledger.
